title: Wringer gate and display proposals
description: A `wringer.gatespec.v2` document — what `wring spec` writes since P0.3 (2026-09-02). v1 plus ONE optional key: `show`, a proposed display command per `human: true` criterion, so the person asked to judge a requirement has something put in front of them (runs 4 and 4B ended at a pen with a blank page). v1 is frozen (schema/frozen.json), so this is a new schema on the `decisions.v2` precedent: every v1 document is a valid v2 document, and both are read forever. Source, not evidence: it lives in the repository beside `wringer.spec.yaml`. **This file has no authority.** No gate in it ever runs, no display in it ever runs, nothing under `.wringer/` is written from it, and `verify`, `run`, `fleet`, `graph`, `deliver` and the pen never read it. It becomes real only when a person applies the diff `wring plan` prints to `.wringer.yaml` — ONE diff carrying both the gates and the `show:` block, approved by one yes, because a proposed display is a model-written command run on the person's machine exactly as a proposed gate is, and no larger a power. `wring spec --send` writes one from the drafted criteria; an offline repo writes the same file by hand and everything downstream is identical.

gates.description: One proposal per criterion a machine can decide. Never one for a `human: true` criterion — a command claiming to evidence judgement is a category error the config loader already refuses. Optional since v2: a spec whose every criterion needs a person proposes displays and no gates.

id.description: The gate id it would have in `.wringer.yaml`: it becomes a directory name in the evidence bundle.

run.description: The command a person would install. Drafted by a model here and executed by nothing until a human has copied it into `.wringer.yaml` themselves.

timeout.description: Seconds. Omitted means the config default.

proves.description: The id of the criterion in `wringer.spec.yaml` this gate would evidence. Required here: this file is the binding channel, and a gate that evidences no criterion belongs in the spec's own `gates:` block.

show.description: Proposed displays: the id of a `human: true` criterion in `wringer.spec.yaml` to the command whose output puts the thing being judged in front of the person. The same shape as `.wringer.yaml`'s own `show:` section, because `wring plan` renders it into that section verbatim. A key naming a criterion a machine decides, or one nobody declared, is refused at plan time — a display is for the requirements only a person can settle. Drafted by a model here and executed by nothing until a human has applied the diff.
